arquivo.titulo: Cleptoparasitic bees (Apoidea, Anthophila) in rural protected areas in Latium (Italy): a faunistic survey through an integrative taxonomic approach
arquivo.autores: Matteo Annessi, Alessandra Riccieri, Carlo Polidori, Maurizio Mei, Andrea Di Giulio
arquivo.resumo: Cleptoparasitic bees represent a poorly studied yet ecologically important component of wild bee communities, responding sensitively to environmental heterogeneity and reflecting local wild bee diversity. Despite representing approximately 13% of bee species globally, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding their species distribution, taxonomy, and conservation status, particularly within the Mediterranean region, which is recognized as a global hotspot for bee diversity. This work provides a faunistic survey of cleptoparasitic bees collected in rural protected areas within the province…

arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Environmental drivers frequently predict global patterns of colour diversity, but whether such patterns depend on the underlying colour mechanisms—pigments or microscopic structures—has scarcely been considered. Structural colour may have different functional properties that result in different associations with environmental variables. Here we test whether the presence of structural colour is linked with environmental variables that reflect potential thermoregulatory and water‐repellent properties. Location Global. arquivo.resumo: Ecosystem services, the benefits people derive from nature, provides a conceptual structure by which to explicitly characterize and protect the coupled human-nature relationships that are central to human well-being, the integrity of ecosystems, and sustainable development. We suggest the ecosystem services concept may complement and broaden the International Commission on Radiological Protection's currently established framework of radiological protection (RP) through intentional reflection on the interconnection between people and their environment. As operationalization of an ecosystem…

arquivo.titulo: A survey of bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) in the Bear River Mountains in northern Utah
arquivo.autores: Lindsie M. McCabe, Byron Love, Jonathan Berenguer Uhuad Koch, Skyler J. Burrows, Kelsey K. Graham, Diana Cox-Foster
arquivo.resumo: Bees provide critical pollination services to a diversity of flowering plants, facilitating the function of terrestrial ecosystems and global food production. Here, we present a checklist of bee species collected in conjunction with a larger systematic study in the Bear River Mountains of northern Utah, United States, over the course of three consecutive summers (2020-2022). The survey was conducted on public lands managed by the United States Forest Service. We collected 8,500 bee specimens using pan traps, hand nets and trap nests, representing at least 199 bee species belonging to 33…

arquivo.titulo: Key to long horn bee species of the tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apoidea, Apidae) occurring in Europe
arquivo.autores: ACHIK DORCHIN, Blandine Rigaut, Denis Michez
arquivo.resumo: Europe hosts some 2180 wild bee species, representing ca 10% of the world bee diversity. The long horn bee tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apidae) is one of the most charismatic groups in this region, and is particularly diverse in the southern, Euro-Mediterranean region. While identification of most species is difficult, a comprehensive identification tool has largely been missing, but is essential for current monitoring programs. This work presents the first modern comprehensive key to species of the tribe Eucerini in Europe. Keys are provided separately for females and males, including 89 out…

arquivo.titulo: Neither lost nor quite forgotten: tracing 19th and early 20th century bee types in the collections of Oxford and Paris (Hymenoptera, Apoidea)
arquivo.autores: Thomas James Wood
arquivo.resumo: Ni perdus ni tout à fait oubliés: à la recherche des types d'abeilles du XIXe et du début du XXe siècle dans les collections d'Oxford et de Paris (Hymenoptera, Apoidea). Les collections historiques sont un aspect indispensable de l'étude de la biodiversité, mais les types dispersés, perdus ou mal interprétés rendent cette étude difficile. Les efforts déployés pour retrouver des types méconnus d'abeilles décrites par des auteurs français, principalement dans les muséums d'Oxford et de Paris, sont ici présentés. Des lectotypes sont désignés pour les taxons suivants: Anthophora aerizusa Vachal,…

arquivo.titulo: Navigating through the high species diversity of wild bees (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) requires more than identification keys
arquivo.autores: Noé Barbier Chabot, Vincent Carlier, A. Perrard
arquivo.resumo: Abstract In the context of pollinator decline and species-focused conservation measures, the need for data on wild bees continues to grow, and identifying them at a species level has become a crucial issue. This challenge is linked to a lack of naturalist skills, to the difficulty of the group, but also to a lack of tools to train people in this expertise, such as accessible, comprehensive, and up-to-date identification keys. Online multi-access keys are designed to facilitate identification, better illustrate criteria, and enable more fluid updates. These keys require a higher initial…

arquivo.titulo: Why make it easy when you can make it difficult? the nigritus group as example of the current challenges in the traditional taxonomy of the bee genus Hylaeus Fabricius (Apoidea: Colletidae)
arquivo.autores: Romain Le Divelec, Christian Schmid‐Egger, Daniel Benda, Denis Michez, Kobe Janssen, Villu Soon et al.
arquivo.resumo: The genus Hylaeus Fabricius is one of the most diverse and taxonomically challenging bee genera in the Palaearctic region, with a confused taxonomy and unclear supraspecific classification. The nigritus species group, currently assigned to the subgenus Hylaeus, was previously considered to comprise 13 species, primarily distributed across Asia. Despite a recent revision, reliable identification of the group and its constituent species has remained difficult. We present a comprehensive revision of the group based on detailed morphological study combined with DNA barcoding. Our review revealed…

arquivo.titulo: The type specimens of bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) deposited in the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, St. Petersburg. Contribution X. Family Megachilidae, tribe Anthidiini, species described by V.B. Popov and V.V. Gussakovskij
arquivo.autores: К. S. Ivlev, Yuliа V. Аstаfurovа, Mаxim Yu. Proshchаlykin
arquivo.resumo: The type specimens for names of bee taxa in the tribe Anthidiini, described by Vladimir B. Popov and Vladimir V. Gussakovskij and deposited in the Zoological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences (St. Petersburg), are reviewed. Primary types of 16 taxa (14 described by V. Popov and 2 described by V. Gussakovskij) are illustrated and detailed information is provided. Lectotypes are designated for Anthidium punctatum ssp. zaidamense Popov, 1948 and Anthidium reichardti Gussakovskij, 1930.

arquivo.titulo: A Catalogue of the Bee (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) Flora in Campeche, Mexico

arquivo.resumo: Beekeeping is an activity that generates significant income in various parts of the world. Beekeeping success and production depend largely on the native and exotic flora that surrounds apiaries. The flora influences bee success as well as the nutritional and organoleptic characteristics of honey, so its knowledge is essential for the development and growth of this activity. Therefore, herein we present an updated catalogue listing the flora important to the success of beekeeping in the state of Campeche, Mexico. We reviewed publications available in scientific databases related to the…

arquivo.resumo: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous anthropogenic pollutants that originate from diverse sources and pose a significant threat to both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Bees are considered active bio-samplers of air quality due to the accumulation of MPs on their bodies. In addition, the ingestion of MPs alters body mass, locomotion, and hemocyte counts without impairing survival. Native bees hold ecological and economic relevance by providing critical ecosystem services through the pollination of numerous wild and cultivated plant species. arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Despite the importance of understanding mite–bee interactions, standardized and noninvasive methods for sampling mite communities in stingless bee hives remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate a novel, low‐cost sampling technique using a custom‐built suction device, the Portable Mite Aspirator (PMA), for collecting mites from hives of three stingless bee species that were evaluated as healthy: Melipona scutellaris , Melipona subnitida and Scaptotrigona depilis . arquivo.resumo: Nannotrigona testaceicornis are essential pollinators for biodiversity maintenance and agricultural production. However, during foraging in agroecosystems, they may be exposed to residues of bioinsecticides used for pest management. Thus, this study evaluated the toxicity of the commercial product AzaMax® (azadirachtin) to the stingless bee N. testaceicornis. Within the framework of the national project Polinizadores: mejora de conocimiento, standardized surveys were conducted in eight 1 × 1 km plots distributed across the four Galician provinces during two consecutive campaigns (2023 and 2024). arquivo.resumo: Type specimens are the primary reference for species-level taxonomy and play a critical role in ensuring nomenclatural stability. However, in the Neotropics, access to these primary taxonomic resources remains limited, hindering species recognition and the resolution of nomenclatural issues. In Colombia, most bee type specimens are concentrated in two major collections at the Universidad Nacional de Colombia: the Laboratorio de Abejas (LABUN) and the National Insect Collection (CNI) of the Instituto de Ciencias Naturales (ICN). Here we present an illustrated catalogue of the bee type material…

arquivo.autores: Carlo Polidori, Andrea Ferrari
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees (Apoidea: Anthophila) are recorded as common hosts of a diverse array of parasitic Diptera species, but information is widely scattered across the literature, limiting our knowledge of global bee-dipteran association patterns. Here, we retrieved published information on 453 bee-dipteran associations to test the role of life-history traits of hosts and parasites on such patterns. arquivo.resumo: Stingless bees (Meliponini) are eusocial insects widely distributed across tropical and subtropical regions, including Indonesia. This study aimed to identify the diversity of stingless bee species in Wasur National Park, focusing on their morphological characteristics, mitochondrial DNA variation, daily behavioral patterns, and nest structures. Exploratory surveys were conducted using road sampling and standard transect methods. Species identification was performed through both morphological and molecular approaches, employing mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase Subunit I (COI) gene analysis.…

The composition of nectar-producing plants for Apoidea varies across different geographical regions, prompting this group to evolve a variety of adaptive traits at the morphological and physiological levels to enhance their survival. arquivo.autores: Walkiria Aparecida Benites, Laura Jane Gisloti
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Stingless bees (Meliponini) are important Neotropical pollinators but remain underrepresented in Brazilian conservation policy. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided systematic scoping review of published and grey literature on Guarani Mbya and Kaiowá stingless-bee ethnospecies, perceived threats, and traditional management in the Atlantic Forest and associated agrofrontiers. Five studies published between 2005 and 2021 met the inclusion criteria; a multilingual update in July 2026 identified no additional eligible study. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Seasonally dry tropical forests (SDTFs) are shaped by strong climatic and resource variability that constrain plant–bee interactions. In the Caatinga biome (Brazil), bees dominate these networks, providing a powerful system to examine how different pollinator groups sustain interactions under pronounced environmental variability. Here, we investigated how social bees influence the seasonal dynamics and structural organization of plant–bee networks in two contrasting Caatinga habitats. Despite that, many taxa, such as bees, is still poorly known in some regions, including several protected areas. These gaps in diversity and distribution represent an impediment in the knowledge of these important pollinators. In this context, faunistic surveys are valuable tools to explore regional diversity, to decrease the Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls. arquivo.autores: Ana Júlia Rodrigues de Andrade, Jaqueline Aparecida da Silva, Mateus Oliveira da Cruz, Angel Roberto Barchuk, Cliver Fernandes Farder-Gomes, Gleiciani Bürger Patrício-Roberto et al.
arquivo.resumo: Stingless bees (Meliponini) are key pollinators in natural and agricultural ecosystems. This study examined fungi associated with Melipona quadrifasciata workers in Brazil. arquivo.autores: Joko Pilianto, Amr S. Abou El‐Ela, J Li, Du Tianxiang, Mochammad Syamsul Hadi, Asim Munawar et al.
arquivo.resumo: Biogeographic barriers are well known to structure animal and plant diversity, but whether they are associated with variation in host-associated microbiomes, especially in tropical pollinators, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated gut bacterial community variation in the stingless bee Tetragonula laeviceps (Apidae: Meliponini) collected from Bali and Lombok, two Indonesian islands situated on opposite sides of the Wallace Line. arquivo.autores: Girliane R. Silva, Déborah Munique Nogueira de Sousa-Fontoura, Rodolfo F. Alves, Francisco de Assis Ribeiro dos Santos, Celso A. Câmara, Lucas H.N. Sousa et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bee pollen produced by Apis mellifera is formed by the agglutination of floral pollen grains with nectar and bee secretions. Monofloral or dominant bee pollen generally exhibits a more consistent chemical composition and quality. In this study, coconut (Cocos nucifera) bee pollen samples collected monthly for 13 months in Maraú, Bahia, Brazil were comprehensively characterized. Palynological analysis confirmed the predominance of coconut pollen throughout the sampling period. Physicochemical parameters met Brazilian quality standards for bee pollen. arquivo.titulo: Field evaluation of pollination efficiency of Asiatic hive bee, Apis cerana under cyantraniliprole and tolfenpyrad treatments in watermelon ecosystem
arquivo.autores: Majid Ikram, Madapuji Rajagopalan Srinivasan, A. Suganthi, Vangili Ramasami Saminathan, J. Auxcilia, Jayakanthan Mannu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai) is a highly pollinator-dependent crop in which honey bees play a vital role in ensuring successful fruit set and yield. The present study evaluated the pollination efficiency of Apis cerana under cyantraniliprole and tolfenpyrad treatments in the watermelon ecosystem. arquivo.titulo: Green Façades in the Urban Climate: Microclimatic Performance and Implications as Potential Wild Bee Nesting Sites
arquivo.autores: Melina Wochner, Holger Röseler, Linda Meier, Leonie Katharina Fischer, Pia Krause, Philip Leistner
arquivo.resumo: When designing green façades, parameters such as system type, orientation and solar exposure can directly affect the achievement of the intended objectives, like maximizing cooling potential or promoting biodiversity. Using data from 22 façades in southern Germany, characteristic features and their impact on microclimatic properties were analysed. Considering the microclimate as an important determinant of habitat quality in green façades, the potential for these systems to serve as habitats for wild bees was evaluated. During the summer period a temperature decrease was observed from the…

arquivo.titulo: Hyperoside Derived from Actinidia arguta Bee Pollen Alleviates Zearalenone-Induced Hepatotoxicity and Oxidative Stress in Piglets via the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway
arquivo.autores: Nannan Liu, Dongfei You, Yunfei Jiang, Tianyu Han, Guangliang Shi
arquivo.revista: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Zearalenone (ZEA) is a prevalent mycotoxin inducing hepatotoxic effects. Hyperoside (HYP), a flavonoid derived from Actinidia arguta bee pollen, exhibits hepatoprotective properties against ZEA; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying this protection remain incompletely characterized. This study integrated in vivo piglet models, in vitro porcine hepatocytes, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to characterize the molecular targets of HYP. The results demonstrated that HYP significantly attenuated ZEA-induced hepatic lesions and oxidative stress. Computational analyses…

arquivo.titulo: The first annotated checklist of the bees of Colombia reveals an overlooked diversity and areas with major data deficiencies
arquivo.autores: Ruben D. Martín-Rojas, Diego Alejandro Guevara, Juan Diego Maldonado Cepeda, Nicolás David Gutiérrez Rubiano, Danny Vélez, Víctor Hugo González et al.
arquivo.resumo: Background Most existing knowledge about bee biodiversity comes from temperate regions, where diversity is presumed highest—yet substantial data gaps across the tropics confound this pattern. Checklists are critical for documenting species presence, identifying knowledge gaps, and guiding conservation. We present the first comprehensive bee checklist for Colombia, a country in tropical northern South America that serves as a key biogeographic bridge between Central and South America. arquivo.autores: Kerdoncuff Guillaume, Boizet Axelle, Mutillod Clémentine, David Genoud, Lise Ropars, Schatz Bertrand
arquivo.resumo: Pollinators, especially bees, are vital for ecosystem resilience through their role in pollination, yet they are increasingly threatened by the current biodiversity crisis. Large herbivores, by maintaining open ecosystems and facilitating plant dispersal, can contribute positively to increase floral resources with moderate carrying capacity, but the effect of grazing pressure and type on biodiversity remains under investigations, especially in protected areas. arquivo.autores: Laurence . Auteur du texte Packer
arquivo.resumo: Six new species of the cleptoparasitic nomadine genus Kelita Sandhouse, 1943 are described from Chile, north of the Tropic of Capricorn, an area where no species of the genus were previously known. arquivo.autores: Molly Mary Jacobson, Michael L. Schummer, Melissa K. Fierke, Paige Chesshire, Donald J. Leopold
arquivo.resumo: To effectively protect wild bee pollinators and the services they provide, it is critical to understand habitat use patterns across a diversity of cover types. Wetlands are underrepresented in bee surveys, and although wetland restoration produces conservation benefits for birds, how hydrological management influences bee assemblages and availability of floral resources is still poorly known. In this study, actively (full or partial water drawdowns) and passively managed restored wetlands in central New York were surveyed to characterize plant and bee assemblages, June–September 2019 and…

arquivo.autores: Tegan A. Edwards, Damien Esquerré, Nikolas P. Johnston, Stephen D. Galvin, Nikkita L. Maxwell, Francisco Encinas‐Viso et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT The conservation of pollinators is of particular interest due to their keystone role in ecosystem function, but is hindered by systematic geographic and methodological biases such that baseline data are not often readily available. Islands are useful as simplified systems to understand evolutionary processes, are known to host higher bee species richness per unit area than mainland regions, and have disproportionate representation of threatened species. arquivo.autores: Fievet M, Dorio L, Gekière A, Saillard H, Alabiso S, Trapanese L et al.
arquivo.resumo: Wildlife is deeply affected by human activities. Evidence-based evaluation of the main threats is challenging, as it needs to be representative of the diversity of the risk of exposure and the sensitivity of the organisms, specifically for hyperdiverse groups such as insects. While bees are a diverse group of >20,000 species, standardized ecotoxicological data for non-Apis bees species remain limited, resulting potentially in the underestimation of threats that the wild bees are facing. arquivo.autores: Scarlett R. Howard, Kit Stasia Prendergast
arquivo.resumo: The extent and causes of recent regional and global insect declines have been heavily debated, raising important arguments, primarily concerning a lack of knowledge on insect pollinators and their population trajectories. Anthropogenic activities such as land-clearing, agricultural activities, urbanisation, pollutants, pesticide use, non-native flora and fauna introductions, disruption of natural fire regimes and climate change, among other threats, are having varied impacts on bees. This study investigated whether dietary BP supplementation reduces parasite burden and influences liver function, hematological and metabolic profiles, and circulating metabolomic signatures in goats. arquivo.resumo: The incidence of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) has been rising steadily in recent years, yet treatment options for advanced-stage patients remain limited. Bee venom (BV) possesses diverse biological activities including inhibiting tumor cell growth in various tumor models, but its underlying mechanism against cSCC A431 cells remains unclear. This study evaluated the antiproliferative effect of BV on A431 cells using the CCK-8 assay and explored its mechanism of action through label-free proteomics and untargeted metabolomics. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Melipona seminigra is a polytypic complex of stingless bees broadly distributed throughout the Brazilian Amazon and of major ecological and economic importance due to its role in pollination and meliponiculture. arquivo.resumo: Seedless watermelon is a highly pollinator-dependent crop; in consequence, growers stock fields with managed pollinators to ensure high yields. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Wild bees contribute substantially to biodiversity in agricultural and urban landscapes, yet the relative importance of local habitat conditions, landscape context, and seasonal dynamics in shaping their communities remains insufficiently understood. arquivo.autores: Ersin Özer
arquivo.resumo: Hymenoptera stings can trigger anaphylaxis and, in susceptible patients, allergic acute coronary syndrome, known as Kounis syndrome. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Wild bees are declining worldwide, with urbanisation as one major driver. arquivo.titulo: New distribution records of two Lithurgus bee species (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae) from Jammu & Kashmir, India
arquivo.autores: P.M. Osman Javid, Sajad H. Parey
arquivo.resumo: The present study provides new distributional record of Lithurgus bees of the family Megachilidae. Lithurgus albofacialis (Gupta) and Lithurgus atratus (Smith) are new records for Jammu & Kashmir region. Detailed notes on diagnostic features, material examined, and precise locality data are provided. These findings extend the known geographical range of both species in the region and contribute to the understanding of Megachilidae diversity in India. The study underscores the importance of continued faunal surveys for documenting the bee fauna of the Himalayan biodiversity hotspot.

arquivo.autores: Kelvin Mulungu, Zewdu Abro, Hailemariam Teklewold, Subramanian Sevgan, Menale Kassie

arquivo.autores: André Krahner, Wiebke Kämper, Severin Polreich, Oleg Lewkowski
arquivo.resumo: Pan traps are an established method for sampling bees across a wide range of habitats and geographical regions, but uncertainty persists to what extent pan-trap characteristics influence sampling results. arquivo.autores: Mathieu Lachaise, Blanche Collard, Marie‐Charlotte Anstett
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Agricultural intensification threatens pollinators and associated ecosystem services through pesticide use and the loss and fragmentation of natural habitats. Sowing flower strips and preserving spontaneous flowers are commonly recommended practices to support pollinators within fields. However, their effectiveness remains variable across studies and pollinator morphogroups, and their influence on pollinator activity is poorly studied in several crops, particularly in blackcurrant. arquivo.titulo: Solitary Ground-Nesting Bees: Opportunities and Challenges for Crop Pollination Management
arquivo.autores: James H. Cane, Margarita María López-Uribe, Rachel E. Mallinger
arquivo.resumo: The majority of bee species worldwide are solitary and nest in soil or earthen substrate (i.e., ground-nesting). Among these, several are effective crop pollinators. Despite their abundance, diversity, and ubiquity, only one species of solitary, ground-nesting bee (Nomia melanderi) has been commercially deployed in the field for crop pollination. arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT While the colonial honeybee is widely recognized by the public as a pollinator, thousands of native bees play an important but often under‐recognized role. Their solitary or semi‐solitary life histories and small population sizes make them difficult to study at scale. Traditional approaches such as pan‐trapping, netting, or larval collection are invasive and may be unsuitable when species at risk are present. arquivo.autores: Jordi Bosch, Laura Roquer‐Beni, Maxime Eeraerts

arquivo.resumo: Intensive arable farming threatens wild bees by reducing floral and nesting resources, increasing agrochemical exposure, and amplifying climatic stress. Ecological restoration using native wildflower mixtures is a promising intervention to recover pollinator diversity and the ecosystem service of pollination. arquivo.autores: Víctor H. González, Anna Dreusicke, Meredith G. Johnson, Thomas Tscheulin, Theodora Petanidou, John M. Hranıtz et al.
arquivo.resumo: Rising temperatures associated with global warming are often accompanied by shifts in precipitation patterns, increasing the risk of desiccation for insects. We assessed the desiccation tolerance of 22 bee species (13 genera, five families) from the Greek island of Lesbos, covering a range of body sizes, hairiness, nesting habitats, and social structures. arquivo.titulo: Local management at low‐ to moderate‐intensity benefits wild bees in European calcareous grasslands while landscape conservation effects vary
arquivo.autores: Ira Hannappel, Catrin Westphal, Jordi Artola, Xabier Cabodevilla, Jelle Devalez, David Giralt et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Calcareous grasslands are important habitats for many pollinators including wild bees but have declined dramatically in habitat quantity and quality due to land use changes at local and landscape scale. arquivo.autores: Elisa Rigosi, Steven D. Wiederman, Daniel Gutiérrez, David C. O’Carroll

arquivo.resumo: Bees rely strongly on visual cues for essential tasks such as avoiding predators, targeting mates, and navigating their environment. However, physiological measures of photoreceptor acuity in bees remain scarce. Here, we used intracellular recordings in light-adapted eyes to estimate photoreceptor receptive fields (angular sensitivity, Δρ) and detectability thresholds in compound eyes of both sexes in four bee species. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Maintaining pollinators in greenhouses can provide a semi-field environment to investigate the effects of biotic and abiotic factors on bee activity, including pesticide exposure, while enabling studies of behavioral ecology under controlled but realistic conditions. In this study, we evaluated the survival, behavior, and nesting of the solitary bee Centris analis under greenhouse conditions to identify the conditions required to maintain this species in semi-field experiments. arquivo.autores: Ivan Nirmalaraj, Nicholas Sookhan, James Scott MacIvor

arquivo.resumo: Bees are important pollinators necessary for both managed agroecosystems and wild landscapes. arquivo.resumo: Bumble bees (Bombus spp.) are crucial contributors in sustaining pollination services in natural and agricultural ecosystems, especially in mountainous landscapes where other pollinators are less active. arquivo.autores: Adam Kelly

arquivo.autores: Zhengyi Zhang, Fan Yang, Zhihao Zhang, Fugang Liu, Mingsheng Zhuang, Jilian Li
arquivo.resumo: Bacteriophages (phages) are pivotal regulators of microbiome ecology and function, yet their distribution, diversity and ecological roles within the bee gut remain largely unexplored, particularly across diverse bee species and geographic regions. Here, we used a large-scale metagenomic dataset to investigate phage communities associated with seven bee species across China. We recovered 121 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) from 132 bee gut metagenomes, revealing that bee gut phages are dominated by the class Caudoviricetes and include numerous previously uncharacterized viral…

arquivo.titulo: Bee Microbiomes Across Phylogeny and Functional Traits: Examining Host-Cleptoparasite Associations
arquivo.autores: Katherine D. Chau, Trevor J. L. Sless, Phuong Nam Nguyen, Sandra M. Rehan
arquivo.resumo: Studies on microbiomes are essential for understanding the various roles microbes play in the health of bees, yet many wild bees including cleptoparasitic species and their microbiomes continue to be underexplored. To alleviate this gap, we analyzed bacterial and fungal microbiomes of cleptoparasitic species with 16 S rRNA and ITS1 metabarcoding and compared results to the microbiomes of their hosts and other wild bees across families and functional traits. We found that a parasitic lifestyle was associated with a significantly more diverse bacterial microbiome compared to other social or…

arquivo.titulo: Optimizing separation conditions for melittin purification from bee venom using molecular dynamics simulations
arquivo.autores: Azadeh Kordzadeh, S.A. Ahmad Ramazani
arquivo.resumo: Melittin, an anticancer peptide, is the main component of bee venom. However, bee venom also contains phospholipase A2 and hyaluronidase-toxic enzymes that induce inflammatory responses. To facilitate therapeutic applications of melittin, these toxic components must be isolated and removed. This study explored optimal conditions for separating phospholipase A2 and hyaluronidase from bee venom using molecular dynamics simulations. pH = 10 was identified as the optimal condition for melittin separation, as significant conformational changes in melittin were observed at pH = 12. Additionally, a…

arquivo.titulo: Co‐Flowering Plant Species in a Glasshouse Boost Both Strawberry Production and Bee Health
arquivo.autores: Sindhu Sheoran, Sally A. Power, Amy‐Marie Gilpin, Sunita Yadav, James M. Cook
arquivo.revista: Journal of Sustainable Agriculture and Environment
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Pollination is crucial to production of most fruits and vegetables but must be managed alongside plant growth and pest control, making it important to understand any trade‐offs between crop management and pollinator health. A key arena is protected cropping, which facilitates crop growth and pest control, but poses challenges for pollination. For example, managed bees in glasshouses may suffer from an unnaturally narrow diet. Co‐flowering plants can be grown alongside crops but may compete for pollinators and thus reduce crop pollination. To investigate these issues, we studied…

arquivo.titulo: Local habitat, not landscape diversity, drives richness and reproduction of cavity‐nesting bees and wasps in agricultural landscapes
arquivo.autores: Sara Tassoni, Marit Kinga Kasten, Thomas Hiller, Michael Staab, Frank M. Schurr, Ingo Graß
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Studying insect decline in human‐dominated landscapes, especially in intensively managed agricultural areas, requires understanding its drivers. Studies of cavity‐nesting bees and wasps with trap nests provide information on the number of locally reproducing species and their potential offspring, and how this relates to local resources and landscape diversity. We investigated insect communities across all major habitat types in agricultural landscapes in Germany using a grid‐based design to evenly and proportionally cover the major habitats of our landscapes. The landscape plots…

arquivo.titulo: Flower pollen sources of non- Apis bees ( Amegilla zonata , Ceratina binghami , Lasioglossum cavernifrons , Megachile disjuncta , and Xylocopa fenestrata ) in southern West Bengal, India: insights from pollen load analysis and field surveys
arquivo.autores: Ujjwal Layek, Arabinda Samanta, Prakash Karmakar, Nandita Das
arquivo.resumo: Non-Apis bees (including solitary bees) are highly valued for the essential ecosystem services they provide, and their survival largely depends on the availability of floral resources. However, knowledge of the floral pollen sources exploited by non-Apis bees (especially solitary bees and subsocial bees) remains limited. This study aimed to identify the host plants of selected bee species [viz. Amegilla zonata (blue-banded bees), Ceratina binghami (small carpenter bees), Lasioglossum cavernifrons (sweat bees), Megachile disjuncta (leafcutter bees), and Xylocopa fenestrata (carpenter bees)].…

arquivo.autores: Rodica Mărgăoan, Mihaiela Cornea‐Cipcigan, Călina Ciont, Amalia Mesaros, Adriana Cristina Urcan, Răzvan Odocheanu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Bee-collected pollen (BCP) represents a highly heterogeneous apicultural product with the compositional and functional properties strongly influenced by botanical origin. However, the integration of palynological, spectroscopic, and protein-profile data for botanical discrimination and functional characterization remains insufficiently explored. The present study investigated 80 BCP samples collected from the Banat region of Romania, of which 45 representative samples were selected for detailed compositional and chemometric evaluation. Integrated analyses combining palynology, proximate…

arquivo.titulo: XHABC: enhanced hybrid artificial bee colony algorithm for recommending the personalized multi-day mixed destination tour
arquivo.autores: Z. K. A. Baizal, Gia Septiana Wulandari, Agung Toto Wibowo, Putri Nurika Adila, Saskia Putri Ananda
arquivo.resumo: Developing a recommender system for multi-day tourist route planning that aligns with user preferences presents challenges in optimization. Many previous studies within the scope of Tourist Trip Design Problem (TTDP) have developed systems that recommend multi-day routes by utilizing the analogy of solving the Team Orienteering Problem (TOP). In addition, prior studies have not accommodated the user’s desire to visit a combination of several tourist categories, such as nature, shopping, and culinary, during a multi-day tour. We refer to this problem as a multi-day mixed destination tour.…

arquivo.titulo: Revisiting a historical plant-bee network from a Brazilian cerrado: insights from a 50-year-old dataset on bee diversity, functional roles, and network structure
arquivo.autores: Leandro Hachuy‐Filho, Caio S. Ballarin, Gerhard Gottsberger, Ilse Silberbauer-Gottsberger, Eduardo A. B. Almeida, Felipe Wanderley Amorim
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees play an important role as pollinators, and evidence of global bee population declines has become increasingly common. While most studies of plant-pollinator networks focus on contemporary ecosystems, historical interaction datasets remain rare, particularly in tropical regions. Here, we revisited a historical dataset of plant-bee interactions collected between 1971 and 1975 in a cerrado area from southeastern Brazil that was later converted by land-use change. Using this dataset, we described the structure of a historical plant-bee interaction network and examined how bee…

arquivo.titulo: Understanding Wild Bee Abundance on Marrubium vulgare (Lamiaceae): Biodiversity Patterns in Relation to Phenology, Foraging Time and Sex Ratio
arquivo.autores: Noudjoud Benarfa, Amri Cherine
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Plant–pollinator interactions are fundamental to ecosystem functioning, particularly in semi‐arid environments where floral resources are strongly limited during the summer. Marrubium vulgare L. (Lamiaceae), a widespread wild plant species in Algeria that flowers during the summer period, may therefore represent a key floral resource for wild pollinators. This study investigates the diversity, structure and temporal dynamics of wild bee assemblages associated with M. vulgare in northeastern Algeria. A total of 337 individuals belonging to 41 species, 19 genera and four bee families…

arquivo.titulo: Anthropogenic Effects, Not Climatic Factors, Are Correlated With Holocene Population Expansion of an Insular Bee Fauna
arquivo.autores: Patricia S. Slattery, James B. Dorey, Bruno A. Buzatto, Mark I. Stevens, Michael S. Y. Lee, Michael P. Schwarz
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Remote island systems with small landmasses and reliable estimates of human occupancy can be ideal models to disentangle the roles of global climatic changes and local human occupation on biota. Here, we explored this with demographic reconstructions of native, ground‐nesting bees with non‐specialised floral visitation habits to infer changes in effective population size ( N e ). Location Viti Levu, Fiji, South West Pacific. Taxon Lasioglossum ( Homalictus ) bees (Hymenoptera: Halictidae). arquivo.titulo: Bee Bread Protects Small Intestinal Mucosa and Modulates Local Redox Responses in Streptozotocin‐Induced Diabetic Rats
arquivo.autores: Ebru KARADAĞ SARI, Buket Bakιr, Şükran Yediel Aras, Sevda Elis Yιldιz, Arzu Gezer
arquivo.resumo: Bee Bread (BB), a fermented bee product rich in antioxidant compounds, exerts protective effects against diabetes-associated small intestinal damage. This study investigated the effects of BB on small intestinal morphology, mucosal integrity, and antioxidant enzyme activity in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats. Forty Wistar albino rats were randomly divided into five groups: control, sham (50 mg/kg sodium citrate), diabetes (DM; 50 mg/kg STZ), BB (100 mg/kg), and Diabetes + Bee Bread (DM+BB). After 15 days, intestinal tissues were examined using histopathological, immunohistochemical…

arquivo.titulo: Comparative Analysis of Methods for Characterizing Tetragonula biroi Friese (Stingless Bees) Propolis from Indang, Cavite, the Philippines
arquivo.autores: Michele Bono, Dickson Dimero, Sean Carlo Palomares, E. R. E. Mojica
arquivo.resumo: Propolis, a resinous material from various plant sources collected by bees, is known for its diverse bioactive properties – including antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory activities. This study characterized Tetragonula biroi (stingless bee) propolis from the Cavite State University Bee Research, Innovation, Trade, and Extension Center, examining both solid samples and extracts prepared using maceration and ultrasonication methods with ethanol as the solvent. Solid samples were analyzed using attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy and…

arquivo.key: t:diversity abundance and pollen affinity of wild bee pollinators of almond insights from a moroccan orchard
arquivo.titulo: Diversity, Abundance and Pollen Affinity of Wild Bee Pollinators of Almond: Insights From a Moroccan Orchard
arquivo.autores: Skaou A, Aglagane A, Tourbez C, Er‐Rguibi O, Benkhalifa H, Sentil A et al.
arquivo.resumo: Almond trees are economically important and widely cultivated across the Mediterranean. Their yield depends on cross‐pollination by insects, yet their pollinators remain largely unknown, particularly in North Africa. This study investigated the diversity, abundance and pollen affinity of wild bee species in a Moroccan almond orchard. Using sweep netting and pan traps, a total of 813 specimens representing 104 species, 17 genera and 5 families were recorded in the studied orchard. Bee diversity and abundance peaked during the flowering phase, reflecting the key role of bloom phenology in…

arquivo.titulo: Stimulus Optimization Using the Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Visual Neuroprostheses
arquivo.autores: Pratiwi A, Jara-Balsera J, Guzman-Miranda H, Suaning G, Barriga-Rivera A
arquivo.resumo: ObjectiveOptimization of electrical stimulation patterns can enhance the performance of visual neuroprosthetics by replicating the selective and temporally precise neural responses characteristic of natural vision.MethodsAn in silico approach employing the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm was developed to optimize electrical stimulus waveforms that evoke physiologically realistic responses in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). arquivo.titulo: New distribution data of the broad–bordered bee hawk moth Hemaris fuciformis (Linnaeus, 1758) in Croatia
arquivo.autores: Lovro Turkalj, Josip Nikolić
arquivo.resumo: Based on the known available records of Croatia’s hawk moths, including more recent observations, this short communication provides an updated contribution to the known distribution of the broad-bordered bee hawk-moth in Croatia. Individuals of the species were recorded in the areas of Strmendolac and Vinine, Split-Dalmatia County. These observations confirm additional southern localities for the species in Croatia, beyond Makarska. Given the limited number of observations, a wider distribution of the species can be expected in the southern parts of the Mediterranean biogeographical region of…

arquivo.titulo: Bee Visitation to Three Clover Species (Trifolium spp.) and Common Selfheal (Prunella vulgaris) and Establishment of These Floral Resources in Turf
arquivo.autores: Julia J Vieira, Casey L. Johnson, Elizabeth M Varkonyi, Howard S. Ginsberg, Steven R. Alm
arquivo.resumo: The main objectives of this study were to look at bee visitation to some common forage plants that could be used in place of or in conjunction with turfgrasses and to compare establishment methods to increase pollinator forage in turfed landscapes. Bee foraging patterns were assessed on four flower species: white clover (Trifolium repens L.), medium and mammoth red clover (Trifolium pratense L.), crimson clover (Trifolium incarnatum L.), and common selfheal (Prunella vulgaris L. var lanceolata [Barton] Fern.) by conducting quadrat surveys on two floral plots in southern Rhode Island. Flower…

arquivo.titulo: Reorganization without disruption: How fire‐driven spatiotemporal changes in floral resource landscapes influence plant–bee interaction networks
arquivo.autores: Caio S. Ballarin, Elena Quintero, Jorge Isla, Pedro Jordano, Felipe Wanderley Amorim
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Plants provide important resources for bee pollinators, which rely on different floral‐resource types for distinct ecological demands. Fire rapidly alters vegetation composition, impacting resource availability and plant–pollinator dynamics. However, its effects on floral resource diversity (i.e. the composition of floral resource types) have never been assessed in the tropics, hindering our understanding of how diverse plant–bee interaction networks respond to fire‐triggered changes in floral resource supply. We assessed flower production, plant species richness and Shannon…

arquivo.titulo: Cherry Pollen and Bee Bread Enhance Fitness of Chaetodactylus hirashimai (Acari: Sarcoptiformes): A Two-Sex Life-Table Evaluation of Four Pollen Diets
arquivo.autores: Zhaoyun Lyu, Hongyan Song, Yue Zhang, Qitong Huang, Meng Sun
arquivo.resumo: The mason bee Osmia excavata Alfken (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae) is an essential pollinator for rosaceous fruit trees in northern China, but its populations are declining because of severe infestations by the mite Chaetodactylus hirashimai Kurosa (Acari: Sarcoptiformes). This mite feeds on pollen within mason bee nest tubes, thereby impairing larval development. However, the effects of different floral resources on the fitness of C. hirashimai remain unclear. arquivo.titulo: Factors Affecting the Geographical Distribution of the Bee Moth, Aphomia sociella, Utilizing Species Distribution Modeling Approach
arquivo.autores: Hossam F. Abou‐Shaara, Areej Abdulkareem Al-Khalaf
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Entomological Research Society
arquivo.resumo: The bee moth Aphomia sociella is considered a pest of managed bee colonies. In this study, its current and future potential distribution was modeled using MaxEnt to improve understanding of the climatic factors governing its range. The model performed reliably with area under the curve = 0.809±0.003, showing low omission rates and spatial agreement across replicates. Variable importance analyses identified precipitation of driest quarter (50–250 mm) and annual mean temperature (3–12°C) as the key predictors, suggesting that the species’ distribution is strongly governed by a narrow set of…

arquivo.autores: Azhakath Viswambharan Vishnu, Chenthamarakshan Bijoy
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Entomological Research Society
arquivo.resumo: The present work investigated the pollination preferences of non-Apis bees in the Kole wetlands of Thrissur, Kerala. The twelve-month study (May 2024 to April 2025) was conducted across six different sites within the Thrissur Kole wetlands. The association between non-Apis bees and flowering plants of the Asteraceae family was specifically examined. A total of 13 non-Apis bee species belonging to eight genera and two families were recorded from seven flowering plants. Among the seven plants, three were non-invasive, and four were invasive. The bee family Halictidae was predominant, accounting…

arquivo.titulo: Mapping wild bee diversity and flower use for an effective conservation of the Doñana biodiversity hotspot
arquivo.autores: Francisco P. Molina, Nerea Montes‐Pérez, Luis Villagarcía, Ígnasi Bartomeus
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Despite encompassing one of the richest bee faunas in Europe, the Iberian Peninsula lacks distributional data that often hampers effective conservation. This gap is particularly critical within protected areas such as the Doñana Natural Area, where biodiversity is expected to be increasingly vulnerable to environmental pressures. Here, we present the first checklist of the wild bees of Doñana. A total of 387 species belonging to 47 genera were recorded, including recently described species and a newly recorded species for continental Europe, Andrena purpurascens . The exceptional…

arquivo.titulo: Diversidad de Abejas (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) en coberturas heterogéneas de Bosque Seco Tropical, Huila Colombia
arquivo.autores: Mateo Carvajal-Cardona, David Felipe Bulla-Guaqueta, Adriana Ortiz-Reyes, Mailyn Adriana Gonzalez, Allan Henry Smith-Pardo
arquivo.resumo: Introduction: Tropical forests are one of the world's most biodiverse ecosystems. Tropical Dry Forests (TDFs) exhibit high levels of endemism reflected in their diverse flora and fauna; however, these ecosystems are under threat from human activity. Restoring TDFs ecologically is therefore essential for preserving their biodiversity. In this context, pollination is an essential ecosystem service that needs to be preserved due to its importance for the exchange of genes between vegetation communities. Objective: To characterize the diversity of the bee communities and their association with…

arquivo.autores: Michael P Getz, Lincoln R. Best, Oksana Ostroverkhova, Andony P. Melathopoulos, Timothy L. Warren
arquivo.revista: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Widespread declines in insect diversity and abundance underscore an urgent need for standardized, nonlethal monitoring methods for important pollinators such as bumble bees ( Bombus spp.). Camera traps are widely used for nonintrusive, continuous surveys of large animals but have not yet been extensively adopted for monitoring diurnal insects. Automated camera traps could improve current insect survey methods, which often rely on lethal traps or in‐person observation. Here we developed an open‐source, low‐cost camera trap for monitoring wild insects and evaluated its performance…

arquivo.autores: Renata Brito, Rafael Cabral Borges, Adrian González‐Chaves, Erlane José Cunha, Ulysses Madureira Maia, Felipe Martello et al.
arquivo.resumo: Understanding how species traits shape ecological interactions across organizational levels is fundamental to explaining tropical biodiversity. In plant–pollinator systems, competition, niche partitioning, and specialist–generalist strategies are closely linked to functional trait variation, which can influence species coexistence and network structure. Yet, how the functional diversity of interacting groups determines network organization remains poorly understood, particularly in pristine tropical forests. Here, we examined how plant and bee functional diversity structures plant–pollinator…

arquivo.autores: Zhiheng Zhang, Jingjue Wang, Dongkang Han, Tong Qin, Siyu Chen, Ruyi Wang et al.
arquivo.resumo: Rice is a major staple crop in China and worldwide, and bacterial diseases threaten its production (Doni et al. 2021; Lv et al. 2022). In 2025, typical leaf tip dieback symptoms were observed on rice seedlings in a rice field planted with cv. Fuxiangnian in Binyang County (23.25834°N, 108.92461°E), Guangxi, China. arquivo.autores: Ryan M. Alam, Danny Kessler, Heiko Vogel, Katrin Luck, Anja David, Maritta Kunert et al.
arquivo.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
arquivo.resumo: Animals are not known to biosynthesize floral chemical signals to manipulate pollinators, although such mimicry could profoundly shape plant–pollinator interactions. Larvae of the poisonous European blister beetle Meloe proscarabaeus parasitize multiple solitary bee species, yet the mechanism enabling host attraction has remained unresolved. Here we show that these larvae lure bees by emitting a bouquet of volatile compounds that closely resembles floral scent. Chemical analyses reveal a complex blend of monoterpenoids derived from ( S )-linalool, a ubiquitous floral volatile. Behavioral…

arquivo.autores: Roberto Aguilar, Sia Mahesh
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Introduction Melanoma cells undergo metabolic reprogramming that suppresses mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and enhances glycolytic dependence. Transcriptomic analysis shows strong downregulation of the mitochondrial gene MT-CO1, which encodes cytochrome c oxidase subunit I, in the A375 melanoma cell line. Melittin, a peptide from bee venom, has demonstrated potent lytic and pro-apoptotic effects in multiple cancer models through mitochondrial disruption. This project aims to determine whether melittin treatment alters MT-CO1 expression, induces mitochondrial stress, and…

arquivo.autores: Daniel Echeandía, Jordi Margalef‐Marrasé, Marc Riera, Jordina Belmonte, Julia Lanner, Sonja Mader et al.
arquivo.resumo: An invasional meltdown can occur when a non‐native species facilitates the spread of another non‐native species in the invaded area, increasing its likelihood of survival or its ecological impact. Plant–pollinator systems pose an exceptional study system to test this concept, which remains poorly known. In this study, we aim to evaluate a potential invasion meltdown between Megachile sculpturalis , a solitary bee native to East Asia that has been introduced to Europe and has widely expanded its range, and the non‐native tree Styphnolobium japonicum , an important pollen source for the bee in…

arquivo.autores: Silvia Gattucci, Laura Canonico, Alice Agarbati, Maurizio Ciani, Francesca Comitini
arquivo.resumo: Bee bread is a fermented product derived from bee pollen, whose fermentation improves preservation, nutrient bioavailability, and functional properties. However, the microbial succession driving this process, particularly the role of yeasts, remains poorly understood. This study investigated microbial dynamics during fourteen-day spontaneous fermentation of five fresh bee pollen samples from different geographical origins, mimicking natural bee bread formation. Cultivable yeasts and lactic acid bacteria were monitored by viable cell counts and molecular identification. Physicochemical…

arquivo.autores: Mateus Lordelo Vidigal, Lorena Lisbetd Botina, Gustavo F. Martins
arquivo.resumo: Abstract The gut microbiota of eusocial bees functions as a dynamic system; however, despite extensive study in honey bees and bumble bees, it remains poorly understood in stingless bees. We used 16 S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize the gut microbiota of Melipona capixaba and Melipona mondury across developmental stages (larvae, nurses, and foragers), and across castes (workers and queens) and sexes (males and females) in M. mondury . arquivo.autores: Selçuk Alan, Gönül Damla Büyük
arquivo.resumo: This study evaluated oxidative damage, antioxidant-related, and nitric oxide (NO)-related chemical markers in commercial bee pollen using two extraction systems. arquivo.resumo: Bee products, recognized for their antimicrobial, antioxidant, neuroprotective, and anticancer properties, have seen a significant rise in global consumption. Despite their value, regular safety and monitoring assessments are lacking, leading to an increase in adulteration. This fraudulent practice negatively impacts the bee product industry by undermining consumer trust, causing market losses, and potentially harming consumer health. This review discussed the authenticity and adulteration of bee products. Authenticity, on the other hand, is defined as the analyses conducted during production…

arquivo.autores: David Javier-Aliaga, Dámaris Quinteros Zúñiga
arquivo.resumo: Introduction: Although several instruments have been developed to assess emotional eating, no measure has yet been identified that evaluates this construct based on the eight basic emotions. Assessing emotional eating is particularly important because it represents a relevant factor associated with overweight and obesity. In this context, the aim of the present study was to develop and validate the Brief Emotional Eating Scale based on the Eight Basic Emotions (BEES-8, version 1.0) in a sample of Peruvian youth and adults. Methods: A cross-sectional psychometric study was conducted. The…

arquivo.autores: Bilyana Stoykova Wild, Belén Gallardo, Christopher Paul Wild, Patrycja Pluta, Mark Frenzel, Oliver Schweiger et al.
arquivo.resumo: Agricultural intensification reduces the diversity and continuity of floral resources, exposing pollinators to multiple stressors. Although resource limitation is a key driver of pollinator declines, the mechanisms linking environmental conditions to pollinator performance remain unclear. We tested whether alleviating food limitation improves bumble bee colony performance and whether agricultural intensification constrains worker development and reproduction. We hypothesised that supplemental nutrition would enhance colony performance, particularly by reducing developmental instability and…

arquivo.autores: Shangbo Jiang, Jin Zhang, Chanjuan Du, Di Yang, Yunfeng Ye, Lian Fu Pan et al.
arquivo.resumo: Banana (genus Musa) is an economically important fruit crop. In January 2026, a rhizome rot disease was observed in a banana plantation in Nanning, Guangxi, China, affecting more than 10% of cultivated plants. Infected plants initially showed no obvious aboveground symptoms; however, yellow to brown water-soaked spots appeared on the rhizomes. In severe cases, plants exhibited stunting and leaf yellowing. The decay was confined to the rhizome and did not have a foul odor. To isolate the pathogen, diseased tissues (5 × 5 mm) were dissected and surface-sterilized with 75% ethanol (30 s)…

arquivo.autores: Jun Wang, Lijun Lu, Peng Li, Xu Fang, Tiantian Zhang, Zhipeng Li et al.
arquivo.revista: International Journal of Swarm Intelligence Research
arquivo.resumo: The rapid development of multi-entity distributed energy systems has underscored the importance of source–grid–load–storage coordinated scheduling in improving renewable energy utilization and reducing operating costs. However, traditional centralized scheduling faces privacy risks, computational bottlenecks, and high latency, making it unsuitable for real-time distributed energy management. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a three-tier “device–edge–cloud” federated edge collaborative scheduling framework FedAOT, integrating an improved Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm…

arquivo.titulo: Wild bees occupy temporally stable pollen nutritional niches
arquivo.autores: Anthony D. Vaudo, Jillian A. Luthy, Eva Lin, Sonja K. Glasser, Anne S. Leonard
arquivo.resumo: As bees' primary source of protein and lipids, pollen is a nutritional resource key to the persistence of wild populations. Because bee taxa may differ in their pollen macronutrient requirements, and pollen is a limited resource that varies chemically across plants, nutritional niches may shape bees' ecological interactions. Flowering plants often offer floral food rewards to pollinators, but also frequently deceive pollinators into visiting without providing rewards. arquivo.autores: Tianqi Zhu, Peter Graystock, Richard J. Gill
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Exposure to pesticides may place the process of animal thermo regulation at risk, with impacts on organism fitness and function across landscapes. arquivo.autores: Emine Dilara Çavuş, Cansu Özge Tozkar

Our analysis encompassed 1040 wing images collected from seven geographical regions using four deep learning architectures: EfficientNetB0, ResNet34, DenseNet121, and MobileNetV3‐Small. arquivo.resumo: Three species of the genus Gnathonomia Pauly, 2005 (Hymenoptera: Halictidae: Nomiinae) are reported from Vietnam. Two species, Gnathonomia aurata (Bingham, 1897) and G. pieli (Cockerell, 1931) are recorded from Vietnam for the first time, while G. thoracica (Smith, 1875) is the most common species in the country. One species, G. fusciventris Zhang & Niu, 2020, syn. nov., is treated as a junior synonym of G. pieli. An illustrated key to the Vietnamese species of Gnathonomia is presented along with a summary of their distributions.
