arquivo.resumo: In plants that offer pollen as their sole floral reward, this resource is finite and nonreplenishable, making such plants useful systems for studying how resource availability across flowers shapes pollinator behavior. Because tropical ecosystems of the Global South harbor exceptionally diverse plant–pollinator interactions, understanding pollinator behavior in these systems is important for understanding the evolution of plant–pollinator relationships. Using the legume Chamaecrista latistipula , which offer only pollen as a floral reward, we assessed how pollen availability affects the…

arquivo.titulo: Analysis of annual honey production in Kenya as influenced by weather parameters and atmospheric constituents
arquivo.autores: Judith Syombua Mbau, Nzioka John Muthama
arquivo.revista: East African Journal of Science Technology and Innovation
arquivo.resumo: The contribution of weather parameters and atmospheric constituents on honey production in Kenya is little understood. We studied the influence of average national diurnal 2-m temperature range, consecutive dry days, summer days, daytime relative humidity, night-time relative humidity, precipitation rate, number of days with precipitation, surface buoyancy, surface wind speed, Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) and soil moisture content, on annual honey harvest. Data for annual national honey harvest was obtained from the Food and Agriculture Organization statistical database website for the period…

arquivo.titulo: God Class Detection Using Thresholds of Software Code Metrics Derived from Metaheuristic Optimization
arquivo.autores: Kapil Sharma, Jitender Kumar Chhabra
arquivo.revista: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences
arquivo.resumo: The detection of God Class code smells is necessary for maintaining the quality, maintainability, and evolution of the software. Traditional code smell detection methods often rely on static and developer intuition-based thresholds of the software metrics, which may not be applicable to projects of different sizes and domains. This study proposes a new methodology for God Class detection by calculating thresholds of software metrics (Chidamber and Kemerer (CK) metrics suite), WMC, RFC, CBO, LCOM, and LOC for more accurate detection of God Class smells. The optimal thresholds for these metrics…

arquivo.titulo: Abundance and Foraging Dynamics of Pollinator Fauna on Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius Linnaeus)
arquivo.autores: Basavaraj Kadanavar, Saleemali Kannihalli, Kirankumar Rudrappa, Shankargowda B. Gowdar
arquivo.resumo: Species abundance and foraging dynamics of pollinators associated with safflower revealed that the crop was visited by a total of 18 insect species. Among these, seven species belonged to the order Hymenoptera, followed by five species of Diptera, four species of Lepidoptera and two species of Coleoptera. Hymenopteran pollinators were the most dominant group throughout the flowering period. Among the recorded pollinators, Apis florea emerged as the predominant species, representing 60.22 and 59.33 per cent of the total pollinator abundance during 2023 and 2024. Apis cerana indica (22.39 and…

arquivo.titulo: Bombus terrestris as a suboptimal host for Vairimorpha (Nosema) ceranae: Evidence of limited intracellular development following experimental exposure
arquivo.autores: Raquel de Evan, María Buendía‐Abad, Raquel Martín‐Hernández, Daniel Aguado-López, Clara Jabal‐Uriel, Pilar Garcı́a et al.
arquivo.resumo: Vairimorpha (Nosema) ceranae, a microsporidian parasite that primarily affects honeybees, has caused concern due to its role in compromising bee health. Although the DNA of this microsporidium has been detected in Bombus terrestris and other bumblebees, evidence of active parasite development in these hosts remains limited. Here, we experimentally inoculated B. terrestris workers with V. ceranae spores to investigate whether the parasite can establish intracellular development in this host. We combined molecular and histopathological approaches, including conventional PCR, parasite-specific…

arquivo.titulo: When psychedelic discourse meets local narrative: Selective uptake of psychedelic meanings surrounding mad honey in Nepal
arquivo.autores: Sharon R. Sznitman, Surendra Tiwari
arquivo.resumo: AIMS: 'Mad honey' is produced when bees collect nectar from Rhododendron species containing grayanotoxins, naturally occurring diterpenoid toxins that can produce dose-dependent intoxication. It has long been embedded in Nepalese medicinal and ritual practices but has recently become part of global psychedelic discourse. This study examined how globally circulating discourse and local narrative practices interact in shaping meanings of intoxication, using mad honey as a case. More broadly, it assessed the analytical value of distinguishing between discursive circulation and narrative uptake.…

arquivo.titulo: Molecular Docking, Metabolite Profile, In Vitro Antioxidant, Anticholinergic, Antidiabetic, and Antiglaucoma Properties of Royal Jelly
arquivo.autores: Ebubekir İzol, Ülkü Yerebasan, E Esin Kayaoğlu, Münire Turhan, Mustafa Abdullah Yılmaz, Adem Necip et al.
arquivo.resumo: Background/Objectives: Royal jelly is a biologically active bee product with a complex chemical composition and diverse biological properties. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the phytochemical composition of royal jelly and evaluate its antioxidant capacity, enzyme-inhibitory abilities, and potential molecular interactions with target enzymes. Methods: The phytochemical profile of royal jelly was characterized using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). Total phenolic and flavonoid contents were determined spectrophotometrically. Antioxidant activity was…

arquivo.titulo: An Assessment of Floral Visitor Diversity and Visitation Patterns Associated with Bauhinia variegata L. in a Semi-Urban South African Environment
arquivo.autores: Usia Matsila, Mokgaetji Georginah Mokganya
arquivo.resumo: Pollination-related interactions are essential for maintaining plant reproduction and biodiversity in both natural and human-modified landscapes. Understanding floral visitor assemblages associated with urban and peri-urban vegetation can provide valuable insights into ecological processes that support ecosystem functioning. This study investigated floral visitor diversity, visitation frequency, and floral morphological characteristics of Bauhinia variegata L. in a semi-urban environment at the University of Venda, South Africa. Field observations conducted during the flowering season…

arquivo.titulo: Influence of cold plasma treatment on the bioaccessibility of phenolic compounds in apicultural products
arquivo.autores: BİHTER CEBECİ, Ertürk Bekar, Esra Çapanoğlu, Tuba Esatbeyoglu, Senem Kamiloǧlu
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
arquivo.resumo: BACKGROUND: Apicultural products are natural sources of phenolics with significant biological activity, yet limited information exists on the impact of green processing technologies on their stability and bioaccessibility. The present study, for the first time, applied cold plasma (CP) treatment, comprising an emerging non-thermal and environmentally friendly technique, to propolis, bee pollen, bee bread and beeswax, aiming to evaluate its influence on phenolic content and bioaccessibility under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. RESULTS: Ultra-performance liquid chromatography…

arquivo.titulo: Tourist perceptions and service design for sustainable community forests
arquivo.autores: Sakol Teeravarunyou, Pongsak Kitirojpan, Kochahem Kamolwit, Pavinee Patanachan
arquivo.revista: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences Studies
arquivo.resumo: This study investigates tourist perceptions and service design at Suan Pa Ket Nom Klao, a peri-urban community forest in Samut Prakan, Thailand. The research aims to enhance visitor experiences while promoting sustainable tourism, inclusive access to green spaces, and responsible consumption. Guided by User Experience (UX) theory, the Tourist Experience Model, and the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework, the study adopts a multidimensional approach to ecotourism development. Three key objectives were pursued: (1) to evaluate visitors’ perception and activity categorization, (2) to examine…

arquivo.titulo: β-Sheet Antimicrobial and Antimycobacterial Peptides with a High Therapeutic Index by Employing the Repeats of a 5-Mer Segment of α-Helical Cytolytic Melittin
arquivo.autores: Rahul Dev Verma, Sariyah Akhtar, Jyotshana Saroj, Juhi Sharma, Mohd Mustkim Ansari, Rahul Verma et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Despite strong antimicrobial activity, high haemolytic/cytotoxic properties, associated with its non-cell-selective membrane-lytic property and its large size prohibits considering bee-venom, α-helical, 26-residue, melittin as a lead molecule for antimicrobial-drug development. Herein, we have explored the design of shorter non-haemolytic/non-cytotoxic antimicrobial peptides with low hydrophobic/amphipathic property and β-sheet secondary structure by using a 5-mer carboxy-terminus melittin segment, “WIKRK”, which contains hydrophobic and polar-cationic residues at its two ends. Three…

arquivo.titulo: Effect of Altitude on Gasoline Combustion Efficiency in Light-Duty Vehicles: Evidence from Andean Corridors (0–4000 m a.s.l.)
arquivo.autores: Paúl Montúfar, Julio Cuisano, Edison Abarca-Pérez, Víctor David Bravo Morocho
arquivo.resumo: Reduced air density at altitude challenges spark-ignition combustion in light-duty vehicles, particularly in Andean countries where fleets operate between sea level and over 4000 m a.s.l. We quantified the effect of altitude on gasoline combustion efficiency and pollutant formation using 94,263 second-by-second records (2021–2025) from ten Euro 2–5 vehicles travelling Andean and coastal corridors in Ecuador (0–4000 m a.s.l.). Emissions were measured with a Brain Bee AGS-688 analyser with pressure compensation; fuel consumption via OBD-II; operational demand via smoothed Vehicle Specific Power…

arquivo.titulo: A conserved miR ‐281‐x is associated with self‐grooming behaviour in Apis cerana
arquivo.autores: Yang Lü, Jiali Liao, Wenyao Ouyang, Chaoguo Chen, Xue Zhao, Yanan Xing et al.
arquivo.resumo: Self-grooming behaviour is a crucial adaptation in honey bees for maintaining individual hygiene and combating parasite infestations. The miRNA-mediated influence on self-grooming behaviour has been recently demonstrated in Apis mellifera but remains largely unexplored in Apis cerana. This study combined behavioural analysis, miRNA sequencing and molecular biology techniques to investigate these mechanisms. We first identified two distinct behavioural phenotypes in A. cerana: strong groomers (CS) and weak groomers (CW). miRNA sequencing of bee brains revealed 12 differentially expressed…

arquivo.titulo: A Memetic-Enhanced Glowworm Swarm Optimization Algorithm with Adaptive Particle Refinement for secure and privacy-aware medical cloud computing
arquivo.autores: Mohd Javed, Himanshu, Snehashree Tripathy, Hitakshi Arora, Tanuj Kochar, Himani Tyagi et al.
arquivo.revista: Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications
arquivo.resumo: Cloud computing has become an influential paradigm for facilitating effective storage, access, and sharing of medical information. Despite its merits, issues related to data security and privacy have remained central limitations to its large-scale adoption in the healthcare industry. In a bid to overcome such challenges, this article suggests a privacy-preserving framework to improve the privacy of healthcare data as well as for securing data sanitization and restoration based on a new hybrid algorithm called Memetic-Enhanced Glowworm Swarm Optimization with Adaptive Particle Refinement…

arquivo.titulo: Modelling pollinator trends using multi‐scale environmental data from the UK Pollinator Monitoring Scheme
arquivo.autores: Claire Carvell, Nick J. B. Isaac, Martin C. Harvey, Robin Hutchinson, Nadine Mitschunas, Christopher Andrews et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Declines in pollinating insects are a cause for concern, yet modelling abundance trends remains challenging and most species are not covered by long‐term standardised monitoring We produce new metrics of change for insect pollinators which incorporate multi‐scale environmental variables into the modelling process to account for various sources of noise and potential bias. Data were generated from three surveys under the UK Pollinator Monitoring Scheme (PoMS) over 5‐ and 6‐year periods, measuring (i) insect abundance and species richness of bees and hoverflies from pan traps across a…

arquivo.titulo: Two New Species of Trichocolletes Cockerell, 1912 From Hiltaba Station, South Australia (Hymenoptera: Colletidae)
arquivo.autores: Remko Leijs, Asaph Whelan, Katja Hogendoorn
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Two bee species in the genus Trichocolletes Cockerell, 1912 (Neopasiphaeinae) are described as new: T. westringiae and T. hiltabanus . Both bee species were found during a survey of Hiltaba Station, SA, a property of the Nature Foundation SA, which was revisited to document phenological differences between bee species. The species are named after the main plant genus they were collected from.

arquivo.titulo: Auxin-induced parthenocarpy as an alternative to pollination of trellised sweet acorn squash grown under protection in fall and early winter
arquivo.autores: Gladys Karungari, Ginat Raphael, Lior Avraham, Sharon Alkalai‐Tuvia, Elazar Fallik, Harry S. Paris et al.
arquivo.resumo: Sweet-fruited acorn squash are a premium-priced vegetable in Israel and are produced under field conditions in the spring and summer. They are also produced from plants grown trellised in screenhouses in the fall, for marketing after storage during the winter months. Ordinarily, in these screenhouses, bumblebees are introduced for pollination when the plants begin to flower. However, viability of pollen and activity of bees are subject to the vagaries of environmental factors. Our objective was to determine if spraying the plants with auxin during flowering to induce parthenocarpic fruit set…

arquivo.titulo: Characterizing optimal task latency in mobile edge computing both mathematically and metaheuristically
arquivo.autores: Mohamed Tahoun, Ismail Mohamed, Hassan Al-Mahdi, Mohamed Abdelsabour Fahmy, Hamed Nassar
arquivo.revista: Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Applied Sciences
arquivo.resumo: Abstract A large body of research has recently focused on minimizing task latency in mobile edge computing (MEC). Researchers in the field have typically posed the minimization exercise as a non-convex optimization problem and solved it either mathematically or metaheuristically, overlooking the fact that neither provides the optimal solution. Specifically, the mathematical paradigm provides a lower bound on the optimal solution, and the metaheuristic paradigm provides an upper bound. The present work is the first, to the best of our knowledge, to explore this fact and quantify the gap…

arquivo.titulo: Analysis of Factors Affecting Costs in Beekeeping Enterprises: The Case of the Western Black Sea
arquivo.autores: Murat POLAT
arquivo.resumo: Sustainability and financial profitability in beekeeping rely heavily on a precise evaluation of unit production costs, hive yield, and regional floral dynamics. This study analyzed the cost structure, economic profitability, and key factors influencing unit honey production costs across 98 beekeeping enterprises in the Western Black Sea subregion of Türkiye. Primary data collected through face-to-face data request forms using Neyman’s stratified random sampling were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Kruskal–Wallis tests, and backward multiple linear regression analysis. The subregional…

arquivo.titulo: Antiviral action of different molecules obtained from invertebrates against avian coronavirus
arquivo.autores: Ronaldo Zucatelli Mendonça, R. M. Nascimento, A. C. O. Fernandes, M. I. P. de Almeida, G. Negri, P. I. Silva Júnior
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Incidences of emerging/re-emerging deadly viral infections have significantly affected human health. For this reason, the search for new products against these agents has become an urgent need. The bioprospecting for bioactive molecules obtained from invertebrates, or their products, sources of research for new antibiotics and antivirals. Honey and propolis obtained from bees and stingless bees demonstrated antimicrobials, anti-inflammatory, antitumor, healing proprieties and several other functions. However, bioactive have also been obtained from other invertebrates, such as…

arquivo.titulo: First record of Aximopsis s.l. (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) from China, with description of a new species parasitising the larvae of the coastal pollinator Ceratina smaragdula (Hymenoptera, Apidae)
arquivo.autores: Zixuan Li, Y. Miles Zhang, Zhixuan Liu, Shixiao Luo, Huayan Chen
arquivo.resumo: The genus Aximopsis sensu lato (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) is a cosmopolitan group of parasitoid wasps, currently comprising 43 described species. The genus is defined by a suite of homoplastic morphological characters and its taxonomic boundaries remain unstable, with recent molecular phylogenies indicating paraphyly. The nodularis species group, which accounts for approximately half of the known species, includes parasitoids of various endophytic insects. While host associations with small carpenter bees of the genus Ceratina (Apidae) have been documented for a few eurytomid species in…

arquivo.titulo: A dual pollination strategy combining perfume attraction and food deception in Galeandra blanchetii E.S. Rand (Orchidaceae)
arquivo.autores: D. M. Camara, Alessandro Wagner Coelho Ferreira, Ana Paula Souza Caetano, Arthur Domingos‐Melo, Sinzinando Albuquerque‐Lima, Paulo Milet‐Pinheiro et al.
arquivo.resumo: The evolutionary origin of the perfume flower syndrome remains unclear. Orchids of the subtribe Catasetinae help elucidate the evolution of this syndrome, but knowledge gaps regarding the pollination biology of Galeandra hinder a full understanding of the process. This study addresses this gap by investigating G. blanchetii, an epiphytic Catasetinae species endemic to Brazil. We explored its floral and reproductive biology, including floral anatomy, scent characterization and pollinator mechanical fit, to clarify the role of floral signals in pollinator attraction. We found epidermal…

arquivo.titulo: Buzz pollination frequency match and pollen release responses in six Solanum (Solanaceae) species along an elevational gradient in Costa Rica
arquivo.autores: Róger Andrés Hernández-Jiménez, Kevin Espinoza-Requenez, Gerardo Ávalos
arquivo.resumo: Introduction: In the buzz-pollination syndrome, bees use vibrations generated by their thoracic muscles to release pollen concealed within poricidal anthers. Flowers adapted to this syndrome have structures that respond to specific vibration frequencies, releasing pollen onto visiting pollinators. Objective: To analyze the match between the vibration frequencies produced by floral visitors and those that trigger pollen release in six Solanum species along an elevational gradient. We hypothesized that Solanum anthers are adapted to release pollen at frequencies that coincide with the thoracic…

arquivo.titulo: Floral intra‐individual variation differs between morphs and is linked to pollen deposition in self‐incompatible distylous plants
arquivo.autores: Renata Trevizan, Victoria Ferrero, Francismeire Jane Telles, L. Oliveira, Lílian Rodrigues Ferreira de Melo, Felipe Wanderley Amorim et al.
arquivo.resumo: Flowers are expected to exhibit lower trait variability than vegetative traits, thereby enhancing precise pollination and reproductive success, especially in self-incompatible species that rely on cross-pollination. This is particularly important in distylous plants, which have two co-dependent flower morphs with reciprocal positioning of sexual structures (L- and S-morph). However, the influence of intra-individual floral variation on the reproductive process has often been neglected, even though this variation underlies selection for precise floral adjustment. This study investigated the…

arquivo.titulo: Pollen niche of Melipona (Michmelia) scutellaris Latreille, 1811 in the tropical forest: a palynological perspective
arquivo.autores: Bastos BP, Santos MESD, Silva M, Ferreira PA, Ramalho M, Dórea MC
arquivo.resumo: Mutualistic interactions between plants and bees are essential for tropical forests. This study analyzes the spatiotemporal variation in the pollen niche of Melipona scutellaris, a generalist stingless bee native to the Atlantic Forest. Pollen was collected over 17 months at four replicates in the Michelin Ecological Reserve, Northeastern Brazil. Samples were processed using standard acetolysis, and ecological indices were analyzed. Sixty-one pollen types were found in this bee diet, with foraging concentrated on a few of them. Despite its generalist behavior, the concentration of pollen…

arquivo.titulo: Alternative immunity
arquivo.autores: Mitch Leslie
arquivo.resumo: A little-known arm of the immune system respond to lipids, with a protein called CD1 driving reactions to bee stings, bacteria, and possibly poison ivy.

arquivo.titulo: Antibacterial activity of propolis-in-water emulsions in relation to polyphenol distribution. A case study on Listeria innocua
arquivo.autores: Abdessattar Hadj-Sassi, Julien Monteil, Isaura Caceres, Fernando Leal‐Calderon
arquivo.resumo: Propolis, a bee-derived product rich in polyphenols such as flavonoids and phenolic acids, is known for its antibacterial activity. However, its low water solubility has limited its use mainly to hydroalcoholic extracts. In this study, propolis extracts (PE) were formulated as ethanol-free PE-in-water emulsions stabilized with gum Arabic. We investigated polyphenol distribution in emulsified PE and its antibacterial activity against Listeria innocua . HPLC analysis showed partial solubilization of phenolic acids in the aqueous phase, while both phenolic acids and flavonoids were present in…

arquivo.titulo: Pollinator Conservation Strategies: The Effectiveness of Agroecological Infrastructure in Agricultural Environments
arquivo.autores: Marta Bonforte, Roberto Catania, Maria Augusta Pereira Lima, Gaetana Mazzeo
arquivo.resumo: This review evaluates the role of agroecological infrastructures, including flower strips, hedgerows, grasslands, field margins, and semi-natural habitats, in supporting pollinator communities within agricultural systems. A review following PRISMA guidelines was conducted using Scopus and Web Of Science databases, covering studies published between 2014 and 2025. A total of 144 studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall, agroecological infrastructures positively affected pollinator abundance, richness, and diversity, particularly in intensive agricultural landscapes where floral and nesting…

arquivo.titulo: Black-boxed ecologies: urban environmental art and the politics of visibility in the Urbanocene
arquivo.autores: Eleni Gemtou
arquivo.resumo: Urban public art increasingly operates as an aesthetic interface through which sociotechnical systems of ecological governance and public legitimacy are made visible or obscured. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies (STS) and Urban Political Ecology (UPE), black-boxing is used here as a diagnostic framework for examining how aesthetic form stabilizes environmental knowledge, political authority, and distinct urban ecological imaginaries through abstraction, participation, spectacle, and infrastructural opacity. Three modes of black-boxing are compared across three case studies:…

arquivo.titulo: Efficacy and safety of Braun enteroenterostomy in patients undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
arquivo.autores: Marios Alogakos, Ahmed Ghani, Stefan Bitar, Georgia Angeliniades, Konstantinos Manousidis, May Y. Hajeir et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Background Delayed gastric emptying (DGE) is a common complication after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD). Braun enteroenterostomy (BEE) has been proposed as an adjunct to reduce DGE. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of BEE in patients undergoing PD. Methods CINAHL, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched from inception until November 2025. The pooled mean and proportions were analyzed using a random-effects model. This review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251160291). Results Seventeen studies comprising 2731…

arquivo.titulo: Pollination ecology of a threatened lupine from the core to northern edge of its geographic range
arquivo.autores: Maggie Blondeau, Cameron So, Anna Hargreaves
arquivo.resumo: Lack of sexual reproduction limits the fitness and long-term viability of many plant populations. This may pose a particular problem for populations at the edges of species’ ranges, which are often small and isolated and therefore may be less likely to attract pollinators. But while many range-edge populations are of significant conservation concern and value, there remain few tests of whether edge populations experience reduced pollination. We address this gap using sundial lupine (Lupinus perennis), a legume that is threatened in much of its range, particularly at its northern range edge in…

arquivo.titulo: Living with Tropilaelaps mercedesae: its history and impact on Chinese beekeeping
arquivo.autores: Liuchang Miao, Xinlan Chen, Huoqing Zheng, Stephen John Martin
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Tropilaelaps mercedesae is an ectoparasitic mite of the honey bee Apis dorsata. In the 1950s, T. mercedesae jumped the species barrier from its original host A. dorsata and started causing problems in Apis mellifera colonies in China. Thus, this mite has been part of Chinese beekeeping for over 60 years. Initial reports of collapsing colonies were from three provinces, all outside the range of A. dorsata , indicating the important role of migratory beekeeping in spreading this pest. Then long-distance movement of beehives spread T. mercedesae throughout China. Several miticides used…

arquivo.titulo: MindVoice: A Web-Based Multi-Dataset Speech Depression Screening System with Pipeline-Aware Grad-CAM Explainability
arquivo.autores: Arjita Choubey, Manoj Kumar Pandey, Ashwani Kumar Dubey, Ãlvaro Rocha
arquivo.resumo: Although speech-based depression assessment has received considerable attention, achieving reliable confidence and cross-corpus applicability with explanation of prediction still remains challenging. This study presents a reliability-aware framework for speech-only depression severity assessment and its deployment through MindVoice. The distress analysis interview corpus (DAIC), extended distress analysis interview corpus (E-DAIC) and multimodal open dataset for mental disorder analysis (MODMA) are integrated to form a heterogeneous multi-corpus cross-lingual dataset of three classes. The…

arquivo.titulo: An Explainable Patch-Based Deep Learning Framework for Marker-Specific Computational Assessment of Ovarian Autophagy in Digital Histopathology
arquivo.autores: Fatma Nur Kılıçkaya İşci, Celal Öztürk, Eda Köseoğlu, Arzu Hanım YAY
arquivo.resumo: Autophagy is essential for ovarian physiology and is implicated in pathological conditions such as Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS). The evaluation of autophagy-related markers in histopathological images is often subjective and observer-dependent. This study presents an explainable computational pathology framework that integrates patch-based deep learning with Grad-CAM-based visual interpretation to enable objective and reproducible analysis of autophagy-related immunohistochemical (IHC) staining in rat ovarian tissue. Beclin-1, LC3, and p62-stained rat ovarian tissue images…

arquivo.titulo: Seasonal electricity load forecasting using metaheuristic-optimized five-parameter sigmoid regression
arquivo.autores: Mustafa Akpınar, Usman Khan Durrani, Kevser Ovaz Akpinar, Asif Malik
arquivo.resumo: Accurate annual-ahead daily electricity-load forecasting requires models that capture opposing seasonal temperature responses without sacrificing auditability. This study evaluates a seasonally partitioned five-parameter sigmoid regression calibrated with Artificial Bee Colony, Ant Colony Optimization, Firefly Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Simulated Annealing. Models were estimated on January 2015–December 2018 data and evaluated once on the untouched 2019 period; each stochastic optimizer was run independently ten times. To establish competitive context, the same split was used…

arquivo.titulo: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Biaryl-pyridine Derivatives with Potent Postemergence Herbicidal Activity
arquivo.autores: Chujian Ma, Changhao Yin, J. Liu, Changsheng Ma, Yajun Peng, Lamei Wu et al.
arquivo.revista: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
arquivo.resumo: Protoporphyrinogen oxidase (PPO) is an established herbicide target. Oxygen-substituted biaryl-pyridine derivatives were designed and synthesized through scaffold optimization. Greenhouse assays identified several compounds with strong postemergence activity at 150 g/ha. Compound 6a retained 75% inhibition against three broadleaf weeds at 9.375 g/ha and caused generally less crop injury than acifluorfen. No mortality or behavioral abnormalities were observed in honey bees treated with 6a or (±)-6b at 100 μg/bee. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and molecular…

arquivo.titulo: Effect of Ethanol Extract of Propolis on Paper Packaging Material
arquivo.autores: Stanka Damyanova, Darina Georgieva, Iliana Kostova, Iliana Nikolova, Vanya Prodanova-Stefanova, Ivelin Dimitrov et al.
arquivo.resumo: Propolis is a natural, accessible, and valuable bee product belonging to the group of so-called bioproducts. Its composition varies significantly depending on a number of factors, resulting in a wide range of data. The aim of this work is to investigate the antimicrobial effect of propolis extract, prepared with 70% ethanol, on packaging paper. Three propolis samples from Bulgaria were used: from the Northeastern region—harvest 1993 and 2023—and from the Central region—harvest 2023. Paper samples from a cellulose blend only and a base paper with improved hydrophobicity from cellulose blends…

arquivo.titulo: A Lightweight Edge Intelligence Method for Student Engagement Pattern Recognition in Blended College English Education
arquivo.autores: Kun Niu, Lei Niu
arquivo.revista: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
arquivo.resumo: In blended College English teaching, student engagement is characterized by cross-stage continuity, multidimensionality, and contextual fluctuation. Traditional questionnaires, teacher observations, and platform statistics are insufficient for continuous and fine-grained identification. To address problems such as the separation of online and offline data, unstable modality quality, and high edge-deployment cost, this paper proposes a lightweight edge intelligence method for student engagement pattern recognition. A five-dimensional engagement framework involving behavioral, cognitive,…

arquivo.titulo: Search-Process Benchmarking of GA, PSO, DE, ABC, GWO and WOA for PMSM Inverter Fault Diagnosis in Electric Vehicle Drives
arquivo.autores: Bonginkosi Allen Thango, Katleho Moloi
arquivo.resumo: Metaheuristic-assisted permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) inverter fault diagnosis is often compared using endpoint accuracy alone, while search dynamics, computational demand, and validation dependence remain under-reported. This study presents a systematic search-process benchmark—not a hybrid optimizer—for the Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). The analysis uses 10,892 observations, 28 electrical–thermal candidate features, and nine…

arquivo.titulo: RAPO-RL-TAC: Risk-Aware Partial-Order Reinforcement Learning with Timed Automata Completion for the Interval Job Shop Problem
arquivo.autores: Pujie Han, Yiheng Liu, Min Huang
arquivo.resumo: In the Interval Job Shop Problem (IJSP), operation processing times are represented by intervals, making machine-sequencing decisions sensitive to temporal uncertainty. We propose Risk-Aware Partial-Order Reinforcement Learning with Timed Automata Completion (RAPO-RL-TAC), which couples Risk-Aware Partial-Order Reinforcement Learning (RAPO-RL) for machine-order construction with Timed Automata Completion (TAC) for execution-time resolution of deferred sequencing decisions. Risk awareness focuses on preserving temporal flexibility in machine-order relations whose preferred ordering is…

arquivo.titulo: Computational Cost Reduction in FEM-Based Optimization of a Magnetorheological Actuator Using Memory Assistance
arquivo.autores: Jakob Vizjak, Mislav Trbušić, Marko Jesenik

arquivo.autores: Paula Bell, Georgia E. Garrard, Kirsten M. Parris

arquivo.autores: José M. Álvarez-Suárez, Henrik Balslev

Monitoramento eletrônico de colmeias.resumo: Network lifetime plays an integral role in setting up an efficient wireless sensor network. The objective of this paper is twofold. The first one is to deploy sensor nodes at optimal locations such that the theoretically computed network lifetime is maximum. The second is to schedule these sensor nodes such that the network attains the maximum lifetime. Thus, the overall objective of this paper is to identify optimal deployment locations of the given sensor nodes with a pre-specified sensing range, and to schedule them such that the network lifetime is maximum with the required coverage level.
